rows.description: As a parent I compare my child because I fear they will fall behind and I feel my own regrets. Wise: notice that comparison motivates rarely, and praise real effort. Harmful: making love feel conditional.

rows.description: I am the cousin held up as ideal and feel awkward, unable to share my own struggles. Wise: stay kind, admit I have difficulties too, and refuse to gloat. Harmful: enjoying the pedestal.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, indifference, resentment, shame
related mind states: embarrassment, envy

rows.description: I stop reacting to comparisons and go numb, telling myself I do not care. Wise: check whether I truly stopped caring or just stopped feeling; then have one honest talk. Harmful: turning off effort altogether.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, resentment, shame
related mind states: detachment

rows.description: I mourn the family I thought I had and feel it as my loss too. Wise: let myself cry, keep routines, and talk to a friend or counsellor. Harmful: pretending I am fine to protect everyone.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, anger, guilt, loyalty, manipulation, neglect

rows.description: I blame one parent and cannot sit in the same room with them. Wise: recognise that anger covers sadness and that adult relationships are more complicated than I see. Harmful: cutting one parent off entirely.

rows.description: I secretly wonder if my fights or grades caused the split. Wise: hear from the parents plainly that it was not my fault and keep loving both. Harmful: trying to fix them by behaving perfectly.

rows.description: A parent uses me as messenger or spy, or badmouths the other to win my side. It is not my job or fault. Wise: kindly refuse to carry messages and tell a trusted adult if the pressure continues.

rows.description: I feel torn, afraid that loving one parent betrays the other. Wise: say I love both and will not choose. Harmful: siding with the louder parent or hiding affection from the other to keep peace.

rows.description: After time I see both parents as flawed humans who do better apart, and I take care of my own life. Wise: stay open to visits and honest with them. Risk: forcing calm before I have grieved.

rows.description: Absorbed in their own pain, my parent forgets my meals, exams, or feelings. It is not because I am unlovable. Wise: ask for what I need clearly and lean on a grandparent, teacher, or relative.
